title: Gates
applies: nodes that declare a gate, Router.match's candidates gate, every node that may submit one

sections.applies: a node whose program declares a gate (required or advisory)
sections.text: This node declares a human gate: submit <<gate_fields>>; an advisory / conditional gate that did not trigger gets no gate but gate_not_triggered_reason. Leading sys.io.confirm/input/select (also in ASSERT work) remains required with trailing prose; unparseable human IO is PROGRAM_INVALID, never a missing gate. Refused: GATE_REQUIRED. <<declared_gate_scope>> <<gate_scope_rule>>
A cancel ends the business work here - Engine.execute-report and Engine.final-answer follow, the remaining nodes do not run - unless this node declares an error route for confirm_rejected.

sections.applies: a gate node when the host captures gate fences, never a sub-agent
sections.text: STREAM THE GATE: write the gate text LAST - after this node's own streamed texts (message / report / explain) and just before the commit - as visible text between a line `:::gate <node id>` and a line `:::`, in Markdown as it should be shown (bold the decisive phrases, `code` for names): the question paragraph (only what must be decided and how the options differ - the findings stay in the Report, never restated); a line `· 说明: …` (the explanation); a line `· 建议: …` (the advice); the options as a table `| 编号 | 选项 | 说明 |` or as numbered lines `1. <label>` - one per option, same order, count and labels as gate.options, the recommended one marked （建议） / (recommended) (the mark goes in the streamed text only; gate.options[].label carries no mark), each with two or three sentences: what it does, its consequence or cost, when to choose it; one closing line `· …` saying how to answer (an exact number, label or intent; other words are retained but require a separate decision, never promise combined answers or an unsupported item-selection grammar). Labels and headers in the user's language (说明 / Explanation / 説明 / 설명; 建议 / Advice / 提案 / 제안). Commit the gate's question, explanation, advice and closing as "@host"; options and recommendation stay JSON and are the menu: streamed option lines or a recommended mark that differ never change them, and a gate text that did not arrive is composed from the options.

sections.applies: every node that may submit a gate
sections.text: GATE SCOPE: a human answer - to the program's question or your own doubt, at any node, in any language - is asked only through a gate, never a User Message plus a default; defaults, earlier broad permission and user_gate=false answer nothing, and an answered gate of this occurrence authorizes no other question. Options: unique labels/intents, at least one execute; aliases never authorize; recommendation = the exact intent you would pick (required, never a choice); advice = one non-binding paragraph saying why; explanation = what is decided and how the options differ. A cancel option is the human's refusal of this gate as a whole (kind and intent cancel); declining one optional step (e.g. skip_export) is an execute option whose intent names that skip - a cancel option labelled as a skip is rejected. For graph branches bind each execute option to next_hint: <declared successor> (endNode for normal completion) - the chosen binding decides what runs next; a cancel option carries no next_hint. Refused: GATE_REQUIRED, GATE_SHAPE_INVALID, GATE_CANCEL_INTENT_INVALID, GATE_BRANCH_INVALID.
